Rater-scored science tasks for the open-ended scoring lab

Source: R/labs.R
openended.Rd

Simulated scores of 1,200 Grade 9 students on six open-ended tasks of a fictional science assessment, each scored 0 to 4 against a rubric. Every response was read by two of eight raters assigned at random, an expert gave a third read when the two scores were two or more points apart, and an automated scoring engine scored every response. Problems were planted on purpose for the open-ended scoring lab; lab_truth("openended") lists them.

Usage

openended

Format

A data frame with 7,200 rows (one per response) and 9 columns: student (student ID), ell (factor, Fluent or ELL), task (T1 to T6), rater1 and rater2 (rater IDs, R1 to R8), score1 and score2 (their scores), score3 (the expert's third read, NA when there was none) and machine (the engine's score).

Source

Simulated; the script is data-raw/openended.R in the package's GitHub repository.

Examples

head(openended)
#>   student    ell task rater1 score1 rater2 score2 score3 machine
#> 1   S0001 Fluent   T1     R4      4     R1      4     NA       4
#> 2   S0001 Fluent   T2     R4      3     R6      3     NA       3
#> 3   S0001 Fluent   T3     R7      4     R8      3     NA       3
#> 4   S0001 Fluent   T4     R7      2     R8      2     NA       2
#> 5   S0001 Fluent   T5     R2      2     R6      2     NA       2
#> 6   S0001 Fluent   T6     R4      4     R6      4     NA       4
tapply(openended$score1 == openended$score2, openended$task, mean)
#>        T1        T2        T3        T4        T5        T6 
#> 0.5808333 0.6000000 0.5825000 0.6275000 0.5908333 0.4325000
